newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Maradona "distressed" at manager's cocaine arrest.
newsitem.headline: Maradona "distressed" at manager's cocaine arrest.

text.p: Argentina's former soccer star Diego Maradona was said by his lawyers on Thursday to be "very distressed" at the arrest of his manager Guillermo Coppola on suspicion of drug peddling.

The silver-haired, tanned Coppola surrendered to police on Wednesday night after a day on the run, following a dawn raid on his lavish Buenos Aires apartment that police said turned up more than 1 pound (500 g) of cocaine in a flower vase.

Judge Hernan Bernasconi, who in recent days has ordered the arrest of Maradona's brother-in-law Gabriel Esposito and former Argentine team player Alberto Tarantini, said the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) had shown interest in Coppola.

"The DEA has taken an interest in this case and we have also received some last-minute information from them," he told reporters, adding that he suspected Coppola had "links with people in the drugs world in South America and Europe."
Maradona's lawyer Daniel Bolotnikof told reporters the star was "very distressed" about the arrests and added: "It's awful, I personally cannot believe it's true."
Coppola, 48, smiled and smoked when taken to his cell. But he told local television from his hiding place hours earlier: "They planted the drugs that were found in my apartment."

Bernasconi described Coppola's flashy apartment -- with gymnasium, sauna, six bathrooms and separate wardrobes for black shoes and brown shoes -- as "a home where it was usual for drugs to be all over the place."

Drug scandals have plagued Maradona and Coppola for years. Maradona, suspended for failing a dope test at the U.S. World Cup, admitted his addiction this year. Signed up by Buenos Aires team Boca Juniors last year, he has also been accused of switching a post-match urine test in August.

Many Maradona fans blame his drug habit on the man who has been his manager since 1985. When Maradona played for Naples, Coppola, a former bank clerk, was charged with selling drugs to his teammates. He is also being investigated in the death of a Buenos Aires nightclub owner in early 1994.
"I know I don't have a kindergarten image," Coppola said on Wednesday.
A man with friends in high places, he was often seen at President Carlos Menem's home and helped him celebrate his 1995 re-election and mourn the death of his son Carlitos.
Media photos often show him with Menem's private secretary Ramon Hernandez, but Bernasconi said neither Hernandez nor any other government official was implicated in the new charges.
